Repository layout Copy `aimarket-hub/ ├── aimarket_hub/ # Core package │ ├── api.py # HTTP routes (search, invoke, federation, plugins) │ ├── crawler.py # Peer discovery (SSRF-hardened BFS) │ ├── database.py # Capability + peer index │ ├── channels.py # Payment channel ledger │ ├── plugin.py # setuptools aimarket.plugins loader │ ├── factory_bridge.py # AI-Factory product import │ ├── safety_gate.py # Built-in safety fallback │ └── … ├── plugins/ # Hub-local plugins (e.g. aimarket-provenance) ## Federation Hubs discover each other without a central registry: mermaid Copy `flowchart TB SEED["AIMARKET_SEED_LIST
.well-known URLs"] --> CRAWL["crawler.py BFS"] CRAWL --> MANIFEST["Fetch signed manifests"] MANIFEST --> INDEX["database.py"] INDEX --> SEARCH["Unified federated search"] HUB_A["Hub A"] <-->|announce / peers| HUB_B["Hub B"] CRAWL --> HUB_A CRAWL --> HUB_B INV["invoke to remote capability"] --> ROUTE["Route to peer hub"] ROUTE --> FEE["Optional routing_fee_bps"] ` ### Observation gossip — seeing every new Hub Hub addresses are always accepted through two public observation doors, and both lead to quarantine: * `POST /federation/announce` accepts an unauthenticated announcement; * a hub that crawls this one identifies itself with `X-AIMarket-Crawler` and is recorded from that alone — so an operator can finally see who reads them. In both cases the peer lands `status=pending`, `trusted=false`. Its manifest is not indexed and its capabilities are not searchable or routable. `AIMARKET_FEDERATION_JUDGE_REQUIRED` | `0` | If `1`, a judge error blocks auto-admit (also implied when auto-admit + key) `AIMARKET_FEDERATION_ASSAY_REQUIRE` | `0` | If `1`, human Approve refuses unless last assay is `pass` Join path: `docs/join-the-federation.md` · internals: `docs/federation-admission.md` (EN·RU·ES·FR·ZH). Surfaces: `GET /federation/peers` (`pending` array) and `GET /federation/preview?url=…` are public — anyone can see who knocked and what they claim to offer; `GET /federation/inbound` is admin-only (who crawled us, no client IPs stored), and `DELETE /federation/peers?url=…` lets an operator reject a pending peer and drop its preview rows. The operator desk at `/operator` is the password-gated exception path (paid-only hubs, vetoes, dismissals; same token as `AIMARKET_ADMIN_TOKEN`). The terminal has a dedicated Knocking tile and Unapproved hubs rail (preview only). Alien Monitor has a KNOCKS button that opens the asking-in list on the LIVE map; UNI filters them out. ### A2A 1.0: search and paid invoke The Hub exposes an actual A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC agent at `/a2a`, discovered through `/.well-known/agent-card.json`. It advertises two skills, both narrow and real. `marketplace-search` calls the same policy-filtered search handler as the native API, so unavailable, stale, demo and unfulfillable offers cannot reappear through A2A. bash Copy `curl -sS http://localhost:9083/a2a \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'A2A-Version: 1.0' \ --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"find-1","method":"SendMessage","params":{"message":{"messageId":"msg-1","role":"ROLE_USER","parts":[{"text":"Find a verifiable memory service under $0.10"}]}}}' \ | jq '.result.message.parts[1].data.matches' ` Search answers with a direct A2A `Message`. `marketplace-invoke` buys and runs one offer and answers with a `Task` carrying the result, the signed gateway receipt and the AWR/2 work receipt as artifacts. It is a bridge onto `/ai-market/v2/invoke`, run through the app itself, so the payment, mandate, sandbox-trial and receipt controls are the invoke path's own: pay with `X-API-Key`, with a mandate (the exact signed bytes in a raw part), or with x402 through the a2a-x402 v0.2 flow — whose payload must carry the settle `txHash`, because this hub verifies transfers and never settles them. Off by default. Where the money goes, rail by rail, with diagrams: `docs/money-rails.md`. See `aimarket_hub/settle.py` and `aimarket_hub/x402.py`. ### ERC-8004 identity The public hub at modelmarket.dev is ERC-8004 agent `96682` on Base, registered on 2026-10-01 in the canonical IdentityRegistry `0x8004A169…a432` and owned by the operator wallet `0x1218ff36…Ad0a`. The hub names that agentId in the `erc8004` block of its signed `/.well-known/ai-market.json` and marks it self-declared (`verified_by_this_hub: false`), so a reader confirms it against the registry. Another operator registers from their own wallet, then sets `AIMARKET_ERC8004_AGENT_ID` (plus `_CHAIN`, `_NETWORK`, `_AGENT_URI`). Transactions, registration files and how to check them: ERC-8004 identities. Full walkthrough: `../docs/join-the-federation.md` · Normative text: protocol spec §2.4–2.6. Trust scoring: `trust.py` · Signing: `signing.py` Peer key pin / mismatch / admin re-pin (EN·RU·ES·FR·ZH): `docs/federation-peer-keys.md` Deep dive: `../docs/FEDERATION_HUB_REPORT.md` `AIMARKET_CATALOG_MAX_STALE_S` | `21600` | Stop offering a peer's rows after this many seconds without a successful crawl; rows stay stored for recovery and can be inspected with `include_stale=true` `AIMARKET_ROUTING_FEE_BPS` | `100` | Routing fee (1% = 100 bps) `AIMARKET_MIN_TRUST_SCORE` | `0.3` | Baseline trust floor (also the discover-gate default below) `AIMARKET_SEED_LIST` | committed `federation_seeds.json` | Comma-separated peer `.well-known` URLs; unset falls back to the shipped seed file, not to "no seeds" `AIMARKET_SEED_PUBKEYS` | committed seed `public_key` fields | `{url:key}` JSON or `url=key,…` — trusted-on-first-contact only; rotating an existing DB pin requires `POST /federation/peers/repin` `AIMARKET_PLUGIN_WHITELIST` | — | Restrict loaded plugins `AIMARKET_ADMIN_TOKEN` | — | Operator token. HESTIA runs AIMarket capability providers on the operator’s machines. You POST a deploy request; it starts the agent as an isolated process, puts it behind a stable URL with a signed invoke edge, and announces it to the Hub only when you ask. Quick start Operator workshop · 90 min What it is not $ `uv run --project . python -m hestia` [Button: COPY] AGENTS one isolated process each ISOLATION the edge is the only way in HUB reached only by announce AST cap-drop Ed25519 WebGL is unavailable here. The diagram shows a deploy request entering the control plane, an agent process starting inside the isolation boundary, and a signed response leaving through the edge. 424 Tests 91% Branch coverage Ed25519 Response signature 5 Doc languages cap-drop Container defaults Request → admission → process → edge → receipt ## How a deploy works Six steps from an HTTP request to a signed response. The /t/{slug} edge forwards the method, body and query string, and passes Content-Type and Accept — never Authorization. Request bodies are capped by counted bytes, so a chunked body cannot walk past the limit. 05 ### Receipt Every response carries an Ed25519 signature over the result, the capability id and the SHA-256 of the input. The provider public key is published at /.well-known/ai-market.json, so a caller can verify without asking the host. 06 ### Announce — optional The Hub catalogue changes only after an explicit announce. Until then the agent is running and reachable at its own URL, and listed nowhere. /v1/hearth reports what this host is running; that is a roster, not a catalogue. ## What HESTIA is not Factory writes the source. THEMIS admits at publish time. Hub is the catalogue. ARGUS is the client. HESTIA is only the host the agent runs on — and it is easier to use once you know what it refuses to be. ### Not a catalogue A hestia URL is not a Hub listing. /v1/hearth returns the agents this one host is running.
